name: Caroline Yates
corrected_note: Confirmed by unanimous voice vote to the Graduate Advisory Council on 17 September 2024 -- a university-committee appointment, not on its own proof of a Senate seat. But 'Senator Yates' is addressed directly and answers questions in floor debate on 1 October 2024 (Resolution 4-24-F) and 15 October 2024 (Bill 5-24-F), appears in the Senate's own roll-call absence list on 19 November 2024, and is addressed a fourth time by a guest speaker on 11 February 2025. No other Yates appears anywhere in the corpus. Internal comparison strengthens this: Kiersten Washington, a non-senator resolution author in these same minutes, is never once called 'Senator Washington' despite authoring two resolutions -- 'Senator' in this corpus tracks real Senate membership, not a loose courtesy title. By 19 November 2024 the Graduate Advisory Council report reads 'No Graduate Senator,' where 'Caroline Yates' had been listed weeks before, suggesting her seat's own title may have been 'Graduate Senator' and that she had left it by then -- inference, not proof, so the seat is left unset. Strongest evidence found outside these 17 files: an already-published Herald article, already cited in years.json under 2025-26, reports 'Senator Caroline Yates' authoring a Go With the Flow bill on 11 November 2025 -- independent confirmation that she held a Senate seat as a continuing member in a later year, which corroborates that the 2024-25 'Senator Yates' references reflect a genuine seat rather than a loose or mistaken usage. No bill-authorship line naming her seat was found in the 2024-25 corpus itself, so this remains real evidence but weaker than the other 19 entries.
